correctness.rationale: For all beta>0 and ordered phases 0<=t1<t2<=2pi, the exact squared distance is Delta^2+4 beta^2 sin^2(Delta/2)-4 beta Delta sin(Delta/2) cos m. The allowed midpoint interval contains pi; strict optimization in m then in Delta gives every diametral pair. Explicit endpoint and Hessian expansions produce the fixed-parameter 2,2/3,1 exponents and constants; the moving beta=1+lambda epsilon^(2/3) balance yields the bounded cubic set S_lambda and total variation through L1 convergence of its scaled indicator. Actual package verify.py passed 4023 checks of raw parametric distances and numerical area laws. Finite tests are corroborative only; no infinite claims rely exclusively on them.

value.rationale: A full curtate/cycloid/prolate classification of the geometric diameter and sharply different phase-uniform random-pair rare-event exponents is a natural, nontrivial statistical invariant of a classical rolling system. Cubic endpoint cancellation at the cusp creates an anomalous two-thirds exponent and a two-variable critical marked law, motivating precise window width epsilon^(2/3). Both the object and measuring convention are geometrically natural, and the result gives exact coefficients and recoverable rare-event structure rather than an arbitrary cut of a parameter table.
